title: Annotatio VI §.I: Indigni absolute — habitual impious/hypocrites (Phil. 3:19)
pass_a_gloss: Now Unworthy Eaters are of a double kind: EITHER UNWORTHY ABSOLUTELY and in respect of whole Christianity, who do not live worthily of their Calling by which they are called from darkness to the marvelous light of the Gospel — described by the same Apostle under pouring of tears notably thus, that they are enemies of Christ’s cross, whose end is perdition, whose Belly is their God, whose honor ends in shame, of those carnally minded, Phil. 3:19 — in one word, all the impious and hypocrites, namely habitually such, meanwhile mixed among true Christians in the Church.
pass_b_english: Unworthy eaters come in two kinds. First: unworthy absolutely, toward whole Christianity — not living worthily of the call from darkness into the Gospel’s light.
Paul describes them with tears (Phil. 3:19): enemies of the cross, belly their god, honor ending in shame — in a word, habitual impious and hypocrites mixed among true Christians.
source_text: Sunt autem Indigni Manducantes duplicis generis, VEL INDIGNI ABSOLUTE & respectu totius Christianismi, qui non dignè vivunt Vocatione suâ, quâ vocati à tenebris ad mirabilem Evangelii lucem sunt, ab Apostolo eodem, sub lacrymarum effusione, notanter hôc modo descripti, quòd sunt inimici crucis Christi, quorum exitus est perditio, quorum Venter Deus eorum, quorum honor in turpitudinem definit, eorum qui carnaliter animati sunt, Phil. 3, 19., Verbo uno, impii omnes & hypocritæ, puta habitualiter tales, veris interim in Ecclesia Christianis permixti.
